title: If only
goal: Talk about what you would do if things were different, what you'd have done if you'd known, what you wish for, and your dreams and plans for life.
intro:
Late at night over chai, the conversation always turns to *what if*: what would you do with a crore rupees, where would you live if you could live anywhere, what would have happened if you'd taken that job in Dubai. This unit gives you the grammar of the imagined and the regretted.

You met the key structure in unit 19: **جيڪر … ها**. The little word **ها** after the verb (in both halves of the sentence) turns a sentence into make-believe: جيڪر مان امير **هجان ها** ته وڏو گهر **وٺان ها** 'if I were rich, I'd buy a big house'. Here you'll use it for the present, for the past ('if I had known…') and with **ڪاش** 'if only, I wish'. And you'll learn to talk about the future you actually want: dreams, plans, luck — and *inshallah*.

vocab.note: Used with ها: جيڪر … ها ته … ها. Many speakers also use جيڪڏهن here.
Subjunctive: هجان، هجين، هجي، هجون، هجو، هجن. With ها: هجان ها "I would be / if I were".
From Persian. Followed by a clause with ها: ڪاش تون هتي هجين ها "I wish you were here".
f. منهنجي خواهش آهي ته … = my wish is that … (+ subjunctive).
f. قسمت سان = by luck; قسمت خراب آهي = bad luck.
f. لاٽري نڪرڻ = to win the lottery (lit. the lottery comes out). In Pakistan people mostly dream of a prize bond (انعامي بانڊ).
m. 1 crore = 100 lakh = 10,000,000. Big money is always counted in lakhs and crores.
Invariable.
Invariable. Also a noun: غريب = the poor.
f. سڄي دنيا = the whole world.
f. Oblique زندگيءَ: زندگيءَ ۾ = in life.

m. Oblique موقعي.
f. Oblique پڙهائيءَ.
m. پنهنجو ڪاروبار = your own business.
f. Oblique ڊگريءَ.
Literally "to go outside" — in Pakistan this means abroad: the Gulf, the UK, Canada…
اڳتي هلي = later on, down the line.
Invariable.

grammar.title: Imagining: جيڪر … ها 'if I were…, I would…'
grammar.body:
For something that **isn't true** — an imagined situation — Sindhi puts the verb in the **subjunctive** (the present without ٿو) and adds **ها** (hā) after it, in **both** halves of the sentence:

جيڪر مان امير **هجان ها** ته وڏو گهر **وٺان ها**.
If I were rich, I would buy a big house.

The subjunctive of **هجڻ** 'to be' is the one you need most:
مان هجان ها — I would be / if I were
تون هجين ها — you would be (friend)
هو / هوءَ هجي ها — he / she would be
اسين هجون ها — we would be
توهان هجو ها — you would be (polite)
هو هجن ها — they would be

Any verb works the same way: مان وڃان ها 'I'd go', تون ڪرين ها 'you'd do', اسين رهون ها 'we'd live', توهان ڇا ڪريو ها؟ 'what would you do?'. Negative: **نه** before the verb: نه وڃان ها 'I wouldn't go'.

**جيڪر vs جيڪڏهن**: جيڪڏهن … ته (unit 19) is for real possibilities: جيڪڏهن پئسا مليا ته وٺندس 'if I get the money, I'll buy it'. جيڪر … ها is for things you know aren't so: جيڪر پئسا هجن ها ته وٺان ها 'if I had the money (I don't), I'd buy it'. Many people say جيڪڏهن in both — what really marks the make-believe is **ها**.

The 'would' half can stand alone: مان ته اهو ڪڏهن به نه وٺان ها 'I'd never buy that'.

**Watch out**: this ها is the same word as ها 'yes'. In ڪرين ها؟ it isn't 'yes' — it's the 'would'.

grammar.title: Regrets: 'if I had known…, I would have…'
grammar.body:
English changes tense for the past ('if I **had known**, I **would have** come'). Sindhi mostly doesn't: the **same subjunctive + ها** covers it, and the time comes from context:

جيڪر مون کي خبر **هجي ها** ته مان جلدي **اچان ها**.
If I had known, I would have come early.

When the 'if' half is about something you **did or didn't do** with a transitive verb, people very often use the **past participle + ها** instead — and then the past works as usual, **ergative**: the doer is oblique (مون، تو، اسان) and the verb agrees with the **object**:

جيڪر مون محنت **ڪئي ها** … — if I had worked hard … (محنت f → ڪئي)
جيڪر تو مون کي **ٻڌايو ها** … — if you had told me …
ڪاش مون اها نوڪري نه **ڇڏي ها** — I wish I hadn't quit that job (نوڪري f → ڇڏي)

The 'would have' half stays subjunctive + ها: … ته پاس ٿي **وڃان ها** 'I'd have passed'.

To talk about regret directly: **مون کي افسوس آهي** 'I regret it', **ان ڳالهه جو افسوس آهي** 'I regret that', and to close the subject: **جيڪي ٿيو، سو ٿيو** 'what's done is done'.

examples.en: If I'd worked hard, I'd have passed.

grammar.title: Wishing and hoping: ڪاش … ها vs خواهش / اميد + subjunctive
grammar.body:
**ڪاش** 'if only, I wish' is for wishes that are **not true now** or **didn't happen** — so it takes the same subjunctive + **ها**:

ڪاش مان اڄ گهر ۾ هجان ها! — I wish I were at home today!
ڪاش تون به اچي سگهين ها — I wish you could come too

For wishes and hopes that **can still come true**, don't use ها. Use:
• **منهنجي خواهش آهي ته** + subjunctive: … ته سڄي دنيا گهمان 'my wish is to travel the whole world'
• **منهنجو خواب آهي ته** + subjunctive: … ته پنهنجو گهر ٺاهيان 'my dream is to build my own house'
• **اميد آهي ته** + future (or subjunctive): اميد آهي ته توهان جلدي ٺيڪ ٿي ويندؤ 'I hope you get well soon'

So: ڪاش هو اچي ها 'I wish he had come / would come (but he won't)' vs اميد آهي ته هو ايندو 'I hope he'll come'.

In speech, plans for the future usually end with **انشاءالله** — saying what you'll do without it can sound like tempting fate.

lines.en: Inshallah. But first — who's paying for this tea?

lines.native: جيڪر منهنجي لاٽري نڪري ها ته مان ڏيان ها!

lines.en: If I'd won the lottery, I'd pay!

culture:
Pakistan's version of the lottery is the **prize bond** (انعامي بانڊ): government bonds with regular draws, and the results are checked in the newspaper with real excitement. 'If my prize bond comes out…' is a classic daydream.

The other big dream is **ٻاهر وڃڻ**, 'going outside' — working in Dubai or the Gulf, studying in the UK, settling in Canada. Almost every family in Sindh has someone abroad, and a lot of late-night talk is about whether to go or stay. Parents' dreams for their children are famously specific: ڊاڪٽر يا انجنيئر!

When talking about the future, people soften plans with **انشاءالله** and avoid boasting; when something good is mentioned, they add **ماشاءالله** to ward off the evil eye (نظر). Talk of **قسمت** (fate) is everywhere — 'whatever is written will happen' is both comfort and shrug. Regret is often brushed aside with a kind **ڇڏ يار** 'forget it, mate' and **جيڪي ٿيو، سو ٿيو**.

lessons.title: What would you do?

tip.title: جيڪر … ها — imagining
tip.body:
- Imagined situations: subjunctive + **ها** in **both** halves.
- جيڪر مان امير **هجان ها** ته گهر **وٺان ها** = if I were rich, I'd buy a house.
- هجڻ: هجان، هجين، هجي، هجون، هجو، هجن.
- Not the future: say **وٺان ها**, not وٺندس.
tip.pattern: جيڪر + subjunctive + ها، ته + subjunctive + ها

lessons.title: If only…

tip.title: ڪاش — I wish
tip.body:
- **ڪاش** + subjunctive + **ها** = a wish that isn't true: ڪاش تون هتي **هجين ها**.
- For wishes that can still come true, drop ها: منهنجي **خواهش** آهي ته دنيا **گهمان**.
- **اميد آهي ته** + future = I hope: اميد آهي ته ملنداسين.
tip.pattern: ڪاش + subjunctive + ها · خواهش آهي ته + subjunctive

sentences.native: زندگي ننڍي آهي، خوش رهو.
sentences.roman: zindagī nanḍhī āhe, xushu raho.
sentences.en: Life is short — be happy.

sentences.native: اميد آهي ته اسين وري ملنداسين.
sentences.roman: umīda āhe ta asīṃ varī milandāsīṃ.
sentences.en: I hope we meet again.

lessons.title: If only I'd known

tip.title: Regrets: 'if I had…'
tip.body:
- The same subjunctive + **ها** works for the past: جيڪر خبر **هجي ها** ته **اچان ها** = if I'd known, I'd have come.
- 'If I had done' often uses the past + ها, **ergative**: جيڪر **مون** محنت **ڪئي ها** (محنت f).
- ڪاش مون نوڪري نه **ڇڏي ها** = I wish I hadn't quit.
tip.pattern: جيڪر مون + object + past + ها، ته + subjunctive + ها

new: ڪاش مون کي پهريان خبر هجي ها!

sentences.native: جيڪر مون کي خبر هجي ها ته مان جلدي اچان ها.
sentences.roman: jekar moṃ khe xabara huje hā ta māṃ jaldī achāṃ hā.
sentences.en: If I'd known, I'd have come early.

sentences.native: جيڪر مون پڙهائيءَ تي ڌيان ڏنو ها ته اڄ ڊاڪٽر هجان ها.
sentences.roman: jekar moṃ paṛhāīa te dhiyānu ɗino hā ta aʄu ḍākṭaru hujāṃ hā.
sentences.en: If I'd focused on my studies, I'd be a doctor today.

sentences.native: جيڪر تو ٻڌايو ها ته مان مدد ڪريان ها.
sentences.roman: jekar to ɓudhāyo hā ta māṃ madada karyāṃ hā.
sentences.en: If you'd told me, I'd have helped. (to a friend)

sentences.native: جيڪر اسان اهو موقعو نه وڃايو ها ته هاڻي دبئيءَ ۾ هجون ها.
sentences.roman: jekar asāṃ uho mauqiʿo na vañāyo hā ta hāṇe dubaīa meṃ hujūṃ hā.
sentences.en: If we hadn't missed that chance, we'd be in Dubai now.

sentences.native: ڪاش مون اها نوڪري نه ڇڏي ها.
sentences.roman: kāsh moṃ uhā nokirī na chhaɗī hā.
sentences.en: I wish I hadn't quit that job.

sentences.native: ڪاش مون سنڌي پهريان سکي ها.
sentences.roman: kāsh moṃ sindhī pahiryāṃ sikhī hā.
sentences.en: I wish I'd learnt Sindhi earlier.

sentences.native: جيڪر بس وقت تي اچي ها ته اسين دير سان نه پهچون ها.
sentences.roman: jekar basa vaqta te ache hā ta asīṃ dera sāṃ na pahuchūṃ hā.
sentences.en: If the bus had come on time, we wouldn't have been late.

sentences.native: مون کي ان ڳالهه جو ڏاڍو افسوس آهي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe un ɠālhi jo ɗāḍho afsosu āhe.
sentences.en: I really regret that.

sentences.native: هي موقعو وري نه ملندو.
sentences.roman: hī mauqiʿo varī na milando.
sentences.en: You won't get this chance again.

sentences.native: پڙهائي ختم ڪري نوڪري ڳوليندس.
sentences.roman: paṛhāī xatmu kare nokirī ɠolīndus.
sentences.en: When I've finished my studies, I'll look for a job.

lessons.title: Dreams and plans for life

tip.title: Talking about the life you want
tip.body:
- **منهنجو خواب آهي ته** + subjunctive (no ها — it can still happen): … ته گهر **ٺاهيان**.
- **اڳتي هلي** = later on, down the line.
- ٻاهر وڃڻ = to go abroad.
- End a plan with **انشاءالله**.

new: منهنجو خواب آهي ته پنهنجو ڪاروبار شروع ڪريان.
ڏهن سالن کان پوءِ پاڻ کي ڪٿي ٿو ڏسين؟

sentences.native: منهنجو خواب آهي ته پنهنجو گهر ٺاهيان.
sentences.roman: munhinjo xvābu āhe ta panhinjo gharu ṭhāhyāṃ.
sentences.en: My dream is to build my own house.

sentences.native: ڊگريءَ کان پوءِ مان ٻاهر وڃڻ چاهيان ٿو.
sentences.roman: ḍigrīa khāṃ poi māṃ ɓāhari vañaṇu chāhyāṃ tho.
sentences.en: After my degree I want to go abroad. (man)

sentences.native: اڳتي هلي پنهنجو ڪاروبار شروع ڪندس، انشاءالله.
sentences.roman: aɠte halī panhinjo kārobāru shurūʿ kandus, inshāallāh.
sentences.en: Later on I'll start my own business, inshallah. (man)

sentences.native: هو ڪراچيءَ جو مشهور ڊاڪٽر آهي.
sentences.roman: hū karāchīa jo mashhūru ḍākṭaru āhe.
sentences.en: He's a well-known doctor in Karachi.

sentences.native: محنت ڪندين ته ڪامياب ٿيندين.
sentences.roman: mehnata kandeṃ ta kāmyābu thīndeṃ.
sentences.en: Work hard and you'll succeed. (to a friend)

sentences.native: منهنجي ڀيڻ ڪينيڊا وڃڻ چاهي ٿي.
sentences.roman: munhinjī bheṇa kaineḍā vañaṇu chāhe thī.
sentences.en: My sister wants to go to Canada.

sentences.native: ٻاهر وڃي پئسا ڪمائيندس، پوءِ موٽي ايندس.
sentences.roman: ɓāhari vañī paisā kamāīndus, poi moṭī endus.
sentences.en: I'll go abroad, earn some money, then come back. (man)

sentences.native: ڪاروبار ۾ خطرو به آهي.
sentences.roman: kārobāra meṃ xatiro bi āhe.
sentences.en: There's risk in business too.

sentences.native: امان جو خواب آهي ته مان ڊاڪٽر ٿيان.
sentences.roman: amāṃ jo xvābu āhe ta māṃ ḍākṭaru thiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Mum's dream is for me to become a doctor.

sentences.native: تنهنجو ڪهڙو خواب آهي؟
sentences.roman: tunhinjo kahiṛo xvābu āhe?
sentences.en: What's your dream? (to a friend)

sentences.native: قسمت ۾ جيڪو هوندو، سو ٿيندو.
sentences.roman: qismata meṃ jeko hundo, so thīndo.
sentences.en: Whatever's meant to be will be.

sentences.native: منهنجي قسمت ئي خراب آهي!
sentences.roman: munhinjī qismata ī xarābu āhe!
sentences.en: Just my luck!

sentences.native: خواب هڪ ڳالهه آهي، حقيقت ٻي.
sentences.roman: xvābu hika ɠālhi āhe, haqīqata ɓī.
sentences.en: Dreams are one thing, reality is another.

sentences.native: حقيقت ۾ مون وٽ ايترا پئسا ناهن.
sentences.roman: haqīqata meṃ moṃ vaṭi etirā paisā nāhin.
sentences.en: In reality I don't have that kind of money.

sentences.native: جيڪر تون هن سان ڳالهائين ها ته بهتر ٿئي ها.
sentences.roman: jekar tūṃ hun sāṃ ɠālhāeṃ hā ta bihtaru thie hā.
sentences.en: It would have been better if you had talked to him. (to a friend)

sentences.native: بهتر آهي ته اسين هاڻي فيصلو ڪريون.
sentences.roman: bihtaru āhe ta asīṃ hāṇe faisalo karyūṃ.
sentences.en: It's better that we decide now.

sentences.native: مان ڄاڻان ٿو ته اهو ڏکيو آهي.
sentences.roman: māṃ ʄāṇāṃ tho ta uho ɗukhyo āhe.
sentences.en: I know it's hard. (man)

sentences.native: توهان هن کي ڄاڻو ٿا؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ hun khe ʄāṇo thā?
sentences.en: Do you know him?

sentences.native: بابا ايندڙ سال رٽائر ٿيندا.
sentences.roman: bābā endaṛa sāla riṭāir thīndā.
sentences.en: Dad retires next year.

sentences.native: رٽائر ٿي ڳوٺ ۾ رهندس.
sentences.roman: riṭāir thī ɠoṭha meṃ rahandus.
sentences.en: When I retire, I'll live in the village. (man)

sentences.native: اهو فيصلو منهنجي وس ۾ ناهي.
sentences.roman: uho faisalo munhinje vasa meṃ nāhe.
sentences.en: That decision isn't up to me.
